I’ll use the skill discovery workflow and search current sources for Codex-compatible review plugins/skills beyond the built-in `/review`.

I’m seeing two different ecosystems in the results: Codex-native plugins from Codex Marketplace, and portable agent skills from skills.sh that can be installed for Codex. I’ll separate those so the install path and trust level are clear.

I searched. Best candidates beyond Codex’s built-in `/review`:

| Option | Type | Use it for | Install |
|---|---:|---|---|
| [Sendbird `cc-plugin-codex`](https://github.com/sendbird/cc-plugin-codex) | Codex plugin | Run Claude Code reviews from inside Codex: `$cc:review`, `$cc:adversarial-review`, background jobs, optional review gate. | `npx cc-plugin-codex install` |
| [Codex Reviewer](https://www.codex-marketplace.com/plugins/codex-reviewer) | Codex plugin | Stricter findings-first review of plans, implementations, and summaries. Low adoption so far. | `npx codex-marketplace add schuettc/codex-reviewer --plugin` |
| [Review Swarm](https://www.codex-marketplace.com/plugins/dimillian-skills-review-swarm) | Codex skill | Parallel read-only multi-agent review for regressions, security/privacy, performance, contracts, tests. | `npx codex-marketplace add Dimillian/Skills/review-swarm --skill` |
| [Review And Simplify Changes](https://www.codex-marketplace.com/plugins/dimillian-skills-review-and-simplify-changes) | Codex skill | Diff review focused on reuse, clarity, efficiency, then optional safe fixes. | `npx codex-marketplace add Dimillian/Skills/review-and-simplify-changes --skill` |
| [OpenAI GitHub plugin](https://www.codex-marketplace.com/plugins/github) | Codex plugin | PR review workflows: inspect PRs, address feedback, debug CI, prep changes. Already available in this session. | `npx codex-marketplace add openai/plugins/plugins/github --plugin` |
| [CodeRabbit code-review skill](https://skills.sh/coderabbitai/skills/code-review) | Portable skill | External CodeRabbit-powered review of staged/committed/all changes. Sends diffs to CodeRabbit API. | `npx skills add https://github.com/coderabbitai/skills --skill code-review` |

My practical shortlist: `cc-plugin-codex` if you want Claude as an independent reviewer inside Codex, `review-swarm` for deeper local diff reviews, and the GitHub plugin for PR/comment/CI workflows. Note that Codex Marketplace says it is not affiliated with OpenAI, so I’d inspect community plugin repos before installing.

The issue is likely with the marketplace CLI’s repo/path parser, not the skill itself. The Dimillian repo has `review-swarm/SKILL.md` at the repo root, so a full GitHub tree URL is the least ambiguous install target.

That error is probably the marketplace CLI choking on the shorthand source, especially `Dimillian/Skills/...`.

Use the full GitHub tree URL instead:

```bash
npx codex-marketplace add https://github.com/Dimillian/Skills/tree/main/review-swarm --skill --global
```

For the simplify reviewer:

```bash
npx codex-marketplace add https://github.com/Dimillian/Skills/tree/main/review-and-simplify-changes --skill --global
```

The lowercase shorthand may also work:

```bash
npx codex-marketplace add dimillian/skills/review-swarm --skill --global
```

Why: Codex Marketplace docs say direct single-skill installs use `--skill`, and full GitHub tree URLs are supported. The Dimillian repo stores `review-swarm/SKILL.md` directly at repo root, so the full tree URL avoids ambiguity. Sources: [marketplace docs](https://www.codex-marketplace.com/docs), [Review Swarm listing](https://www.codex-marketplace.com/plugins/dimillian-skills-review-swarm), [GitHub folder](https://github.com/Dimillian/Skills/tree/main/review-swarm).

can i use as slash commands?
I’ll verify the installed skill metadata so I can answer based on how these were installed, not just the marketplace wording.

Not as `/review-swarm` by default. What we installed are Codex **skills**, not slash-command plugins.

After restarting Codex, invoke them by name in a prompt, for example:

```text
Use review-swarm to review my current git diff.
```

or explicitly:

```text
$review-swarm review the current diff
```

```text
$review-and-simplify-changes review my changed code
```

For safe cleanup mode:

```text
$review-and-simplify-changes simplify my current changes and run relevant validation
```

Slash commands like `/review-swarm` only work if something installs an actual slash command. These two installs only added `SKILL.md` skill directories under `~/.codex/skills`.
what are plugins for review i can invoke with slash command
I’ll check the current Codex Marketplace/docs and local plugin layout so I can distinguish true slash-command plugins from skills that only trigger by name.

Short answer: **Codex plugins do not get their own `/plugin-name` slash commands**. In Codex CLI, slash commands are built-ins like `/review` and `/plugins`. Installed plugins are invoked with `@plugin` or bundled skills with `$skill`.

Use slash commands like this:

```text
/review        # built-in Codex review
/plugins       # browse/install/toggle plugins
/skills        # if your Codex build exposes it, choose installed skills
```

Review-related plugins worth using:

| Plugin | Best for | Install |
|---|---|---|
| [GitHub](https://www.codex-marketplace.com/plugins/github) | PR review, review comments, CI failures | `npx codex-marketplace add openai/plugins/plugins/github --plugin --global` |
| [Codex Reviewer](https://www.codex-marketplace.com/plugins/codex-reviewer) | stricter second-pass review | `npx codex-marketplace add schuettc/codex-reviewer --plugin --global` |
| [HOTL](https://www.codex-marketplace.com/plugins/hotl) | plan, execute, review, verify workflow | `npx codex-marketplace add yimwoo/hotl-plugin --plugin --global` |
| [Brooks Lint](https://www.codex-marketplace.com/plugins/brooks-lint) | architecture, tech debt, test-quality review | `npx codex-marketplace add hyhmrright/brooks-lint --plugin --global` |
| [ATeam](https://www.codex-marketplace.com/plugins/ateam) | specialist `@Reviewer` role | `npx codex-marketplace add yimwoo/codex-agenteam --plugin --global` |
| [Build Web Apps](https://www.codex-marketplace.com/plugins/build-web-apps) | web/UI review, React/Next guidance | `npx codex-marketplace add openai/plugins/plugins/build-web-apps --plugin --global` |

After install/restart, invoke with examples like:

```text
@codex-reviewer review my current diff
@github review this PR
@Reviewer review the implementation
$review-swarm review my current diff
```

Source note: OpenAI’s Codex docs say `/plugins` is the slash command for plugin browsing, while plugins/skills are explicitly invoked with `@` or `$`, not custom slash commands. See [Codex slash commands](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/slash-commands) and [Codex plugins](https://developers.openai.com/codex/plugins).
